name: Blue-throated Barbet
description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread permanent resident; loud repetitive calls in spring/summer. The size of the bird is 20-23 cm. Chunky green forest bird with a heavy tufted bill and colorful head patterns. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Blue-throated Flycatcher
description: Assam Seasonality: Summer breeding visitor from April to September, with some resident populations in the foothills. Measures 14-15 cm. A small, compact flycatcher typically found in the forest understory. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male features deep blue upperparts, a dark blue throat, and a bright rusty-orange breast. The female is plain olive-brown above and pale buff below, lacking the blue and orange plumage entirely.

name: Blue-winged Leafbird
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in broadleaved forests and wooded edges. Measures 16.5-18.5 cm. A vibrant, leaf-green canopy bird with striking turquoise-blue patches on the edges of its wing and tail feathers. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has a solid black face mask and throat bordered by yellow. The female has a completely green throat (lacking the black mask) and a faint bluish jawline streak.

name: Blue-winged Minla
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident, mostly found in mid-to-high elevation hill forests. Measures 15 cm. It has a brownish-grey body, pale whitish underparts, and distinct, brilliant blue edging on its wings and tail feathers. It often shows a slightly peaked crown. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar with no obvious visual differences.

name: Bluethroat
description: Assam Seasonality: Common winter visitor (Oct-Apr) foraging on ground in marshy edges and wet fields. The size of the bird is 13-15 cm. Terrestrial chat with a prominent white supercilium and longish legs. Dimorphism: Strongly dimorphic; breeding male boasts a brilliant blue throat patch with a central red/white spot, absent in females.

name: Blunt-winged Warbler
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor to tall reeds, elephant grass and wetland edges (November to March). Identification: Measures 13–14 cm. A plain, unstreaked warm-brown warbler with pale buff underparts and relatively short, rounded wings. It looks very similar to the Blyth's Reed Warbler but has a noticeably shorter, stubbier bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Blyth's Kingfisher
description: Presence in Assam: Very rare, secretive year-round resident along fast-flowing, shaded streams in dense, hilly evergreen forests. Identification: Measures 22-23 cm. It looks like a supersized version of the Common Kingfisher. It has brilliant deep blue upperparts, bright rufous-orange underparts and a blackish ear covert. Its massive size is the best field mark. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic primarily by the bill. The male has an entirely black bill. The female has a black upper bill but a dull reddish/orange lower bill.

name: Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher
description: Assam Seasonality: Mix of altitudinal summer breeders and winter migrants. The size of the bird is 22-25 cm (excuding tail). Small upright-perching insectivore that sally-catches flies. Dimorphism: Strikingly dimorphic; males are brightly colored (blue, orange, or white), females are dull brown/grey.

name: Blyth's Pipit
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor to dry, open plains and short grasslands (November to March). Identification: Measures 15–17 cm. A streaky, warm-brown ground-dwelling bird with pale buffy underparts. It looks nearly identical to the Richard's Pipit but has a slightly shorter bill, a less upright stance and a different complex pattern on its wing feathers (median coverts). Often identified definitively by its harsh "pshee" flight call. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Blyth's Reed Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: A widespread winter visitor found in bushes and scrublands from September to April. Measures 13–14 cm. A plain, unstreaked olive-brown warbler with pale underparts, a relatively long and pointed bill, and a faint pale eyebrow (supercilium). Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Brahminy Kite
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 44-52 cm. name: Brahminy Starling
description: Assam Seasonality: A very rare visitor in the across all habitats. The size of the bird is 19-21 cm. Robust, highly vocal omnivorous bird with sturdy yellow or pale legs. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Bristled Grassbird
description: Assam Seasonality: Rare summer visitor, dependent entirely on tall, wet grasslands. Measures 19-21 cm. A robust, heavy-set grass warbler. It has heavily dark-streaked brown upperparts, a thick bill, a long graduated tail, and stiff, bristly feathers around the base of the bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 29-31 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident; conspicuous perching on open branches. The size of the bird is 23-25 cm. Glossy black plumage with a distinctively forked or modified tail. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes are identical.

description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 22-25 cm. description: Assam Seasonality: Permanent nocturnal resident. The size of the bird is 48-55 cm. Nocturnal predator with a large facial disc, forward-facing eyes, and silent flight. Dimorphism: Plumage is identical; females are frequently larger and heavier.

description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread; some are winter visitors (Oct-April). The size of the bird is 18-20 cm. Hooked carnivorous bill, distinct black eye-mask. Dimorphism: Males have starker, darker masks; females often show faint scalloping on underparts.

description: Assam Seasonality: Permanent nocturnal resident. The size of the bird is 45-57 cm. Nocturnal predator with a large facial disc, forward-facing eyes, and silent flight. Dimorphism: Plumage is identical; females are frequently larger and heavier.

name: Brown-backed Needletail
description: Presence in Assam: Year-round resident and summer visitor, hunting high over broadleaved evergreen forests. Identification: Measures 23–25 cm. An enormous swift. It is blackish-brown overall with a pale brown saddle on its back and dark underparts. Crucially, it has prominent bright white spots between the bill and the eye (loral spots). Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Brown-breasted Flycatcher
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly passage migrant or localized summer breeder (April to September). Measures 13–14 cm. Olive-brown upperparts and a pale throat. Its key field mark is a very distinct pale-brown wash across the breast that contrasts sharply with a pure white throat and center belly. It also has a distinct white eye-ring. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Brown-cheeked Fulvetta
description: Presence in Assam: Year-round resident in the undergrowth of mixed and bamboo forests. Identification: Measures 15–16.5 cm. A drab, small understory bird. It has a greyish crown, an olive-brown back, and pale buffy underparts. It gets its name from a distinct dark brownish wash on its cheeks, and it lacks the dark lateral crown stripes seen in similar fulvettas. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Buff Barred Warbler
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor from the high Himalayas, found in foothill canopies from October to March. Identification: Measures 10–11 cm. A tiny leaf warbler. It is dark olive above and dull yellow below, featuring a distinct pale yellow eyebrow, prominent bright orange-buff wingbars and white outer tail feathers that flash when it moves. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Burmese Shrike
description: Presence in Assam: A very rare winter visitor and passage migrant, occasionally found in open scrub and edges from November to March. Identification: Measures 19–20 cm. It features a dark grey crown, a rich chestnut-red back (mantle), a bold black mask through the eyes, and clean white underparts. Male vs. Female: Slightly dimorphic. The female has a slightly duller, browner face mask and duller chestnut upperparts compared to the male's crisp black-and-chestnut contrast.

name: Cattle Egret
description: Assam Seasonality: Common year-round resident; develops ornamental plumes in breeding season (May-Aug). The size of the bird is 46-56 cm. Long-legged, long-necked wading bird found around wetlands. Dimorphism: Sexes are generally identical.

name: Changeable Hawk Eagle
description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread year-round resident in broadleaved forests and wooded edges. The size of the bird is 60-72 cm. Large, slender eagle appearing in dark or pale morphs, often with a prominent crest. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes are similar in plumage, but females are noticeably larger and heavier.

name: Chestnut headed-Tesia
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor and altitudinal migrant; descends to lower hill undergrowth from November to March. Identification: Measures 9-10 cm. A tiny, tailless understory bird. It is unmistakable: it has a bright chestnut-red head, olive-green upperparts, and glowing, bright yellow underparts. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Chestnut Munia
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 11-12 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Chestnut-bellied Nuthatch
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 12-13 cm. name: Chestnut-bellied Rock Thrush
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident in higher hills, dropping to lower foothill elevations as a winter visitor (October to April). Measures 21-23 cm. A relatively large, robust forest thrush. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. The male is bright cobalt-blue above with a dark face mask and deep chestnut-red underparts. The female is heavily scaled with grey-brown above and pale below, with a distinct pale buffy crescent behind her eye.

name: Chestnut-capped Babbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Highly sedentary year-round resident. The size of the bird is 17-20 cm. Gregarious forest/undergrowth bird with strong legs, operating in noisy social flocks. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Chestnut-crowned Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in broadleaved hill forests. Measures 10–11 cm. A tiny, hyperactive canopy warbler. It features a bright chestnut crown, a grey face with broken white eye-rings, an olive-green back, and bright yellow underparts. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Chestnut-eared Bunting
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor to grasslands, scrub, and agricultural edges (November to March). Measures 16 cm. A streaky brownish bird notable for its chestnut-colored cheeks (ear coverts) and a black-streaked "necklace" across the upper breast over a white throat. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has a greyer crown and much brighter, bolder chestnut cheeks and breast streaking. The female is duller, heavily streaked, with washed-out cheek patches.

name: Chestnut-headed Bee-eater
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 18-22 cm. name: Chestnut-tailed Minla
description: Presence in Assam: Resident in high-elevation hills, descending to lower foothill forests in winter (November to March). Identification: Measures 16–18 cm. An intricately patterned canopy bird. It has olive-grey upperparts, a scaly throat, an orange-rufous crown, striking black-and-yellow barring on the wings, and a distinctly rusty-orange tail. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Chestnut-tailed Starling
description: Assam Seasonality: Very common permanent resident across all habitats. The size of the bird is 20-22 cm. Robust, highly vocal omnivorous bird with sturdy yellow or pale legs. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Chestnut-winged Cuckoo
description: Assam Seasonality: Summer breeding migrant (Apr-Sep) favoring scrub jungles and deciduous forest edges. The size of the bird is 39-47 cm. Striking crested cuckoo with a glossy black head, chestnut wings, and white half-collar. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes are identical in size and plumage.

name: Chinese Pond Heron
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare summer visitor; develops ornamental plumes in breeding season (May-Aug). The size of the bird is 45-52 cm. Long-legged, long-necked wading bird found around wetlands. Dimorphism: Sexes are generally identical.

name: Cinnamon Bittern
description: Assam Seasonality: Common year-round resident; develops ornamental plumes in breeding season (May-Aug). The size of the bird is 38-40 cm. Long-legged, long-necked wading bird found around wetlands. Dimorphism: Sexes are generally identical.

name: Citrine Wagtail
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly winter visitors (Oct-April) found in grasslands and riverbanks. The size of the bird is 16-20 cm. Slender terrestrial bird that walks on the ground and constantly pumps its tail. Dimorphism: Sexes are largely identical.

name: Clamorous Reed Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident and winter visitor occupying dense reedbeds around lakes and large wetlands. The size of the bird is 18-20 cm. Large, unstreaked brown warbler with a long, heavy bill and steep forehead. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes identical, primarily identified by their loud, harsh, grating songs.

name: Collared Falconet
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident in open deciduous forests, frequently perching on high dead treetops to hunt. The size of the bird is 17-19 cm. Tiny, shrike-like falcon with a black-and-white head, white collar, and rufous-washed underparts. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes are identical in plumage and markings.

name: Collared owlet
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident in broadleaved evergreen and deciduous hill forests. The size of the bird is 15-17 cm. Extremely small owl with a rounded head, yellow eyes, and false eyespots on the nape. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes identical in their finely barred brown-and-white plumage.

name: Collared Scops-Owl
description: Assam Seasonality: Common year-round resident in broadleaved forests, edges, and wooded villages. The size of the bird is 23-25 cm. Small owl with distinct ear tufts, dark eyes, and a prominent pale collar on the hindneck. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; plumage is identical, heavily camouflaged with bark-like mottling.

name: Common Cuckoo
description: Assam Seasonality: Summer breeding visitor (April to August). Measures 32–34 cm. A slender, hawk-like bird with long, pointed wings. It has ash-grey upperparts, a grey upper breast, and prominent black-and-white barring on the lower breast and belly. Male vs. Female: Mostly dimorphic. Males are uniformly grey above. Most females resemble males but have a pale rufous wash on the breast, while some are "rufous morphs" (entirely reddish-brown and barred).

name: Common Goldeneye
description: Presence in Assam: Extremely rare winter vagrant to major water bodies. Identification: Measures 40–51 cm. A compact diving duck with a distinctively peaked, triangular head. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. The male has a bright white body with a black back, a dark iridescent green head and a brilliant, large round white spot on the cheek just directly in front of the eye. The female has a grey body, a chocolate-brown head and a pale collar, lacking the white facial spot.

name: Common Green Magpie
description: Presence in Assam: Year-round resident in the dense canopy and understory of broadleaved forests. Identification: Measures 37–39 cm. A stunning, bright apple-green bird with a bold black mask through striking reddish eyes, contrasting chestnut-red wings, and a long, graduated green tail with white tips. (Note: The green pigment fades to pale blue if exposed to too much direct sunlight or in captivity). Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Common Greenshank
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 30-34 cm. The adult male has a brilliant carmine-red head, breast, and rump. The female (and young males) are uniformly drab, streaky olive-brown with no red coloration at all.

name: Common Sandpiper
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 18-20 cm. name: Common Snipe
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's inland water bodies. The size of the bird is 25-28 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Common Starling / European Starling
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor, mostly restricted to the western and central plains of Assam (November to March). Measures 21–22 cm. A stocky, short-tailed bird. In winter plumage (when in Assam), it is glossy black with iridescent purple/green tones, heavily speckled with prominent white and buff spots, with a dark bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are visually similar.

name: Common Tailorbird
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 10-14 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Common Woodshrike
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in open woodlands and scrub. Measures 13-18 cm. A drab, ashy-brown bird with a distinct broad white eyebrow (supercilium) bordered directly below by a dark eye-stripe or mask. It frequently flashes white outer tail feathers in flight. Male vs. Female: Sexes are nearly identical.

name: Coppersmith Barbet
description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread permanent resident; loud repetitive calls in spring/summer. The size of the bird is 15-17 cm. Chunky green forest bird with a heavy tufted bill and colorful head patterns. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Cotton Pygmy Goose
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident on inland water bodies. The size of the bird is 26-30 cm. Aquatic waterfowl with webbed feet and a flattened bill. Dimorphism: Strongly dimorphic in breeding season; males display bright ornamental plumage, females are cryptically mottled brown.

name: Crested Bunting
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident and altitudinal migrant; moves to lower elevations in winter. Measures around 15 cm. Easily recognizable by its very prominent, upright, pointed head crest. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. The male is pitch-black overall with sharply contrasting rich chestnut wings and tail. The female is drab, streaky olive-brown, but retains the distinct crest and a faint rufous wash on the wings.

name: Crested Goshawk
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident occupying the mid-canopy of tropical broadleaved forests. The size of the bird is 30-46 cm. Medium raptor with a short crest, barred underparts, and a distinct dark mesial stripe on the throat. Dimorphism: Male has a greyer head and finer barring; female is browner with broader streaks.

name: Crested Kingfisher
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare year-round resident along fast-flowing, rocky rivers in the foothills. Measures 41–43 cm. The largest kingfisher in the region. It is entirely black and white, covered in intricate speckles and barring, with a massive, shaggy crest and a huge, thick dark bill. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has a faint rufous (rusty-red) wash hidden under the wings and on its breast band. The female lacks this rufous wash entirely.

name: Crested Serpent Eagle
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 55-75 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Crested Treeswift
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in open deciduous forests and edges, often seen perching on high bare branches. The size of the bird is 23-25 cm. Sleek, deeply forked-tailed aerial bird with a prominent crest on the forehead and grey plumage. Dimorphism: Male features a diagnostic chestnut-red ear covert/cheek patch; female's cheek is dark grey.

name: Crimson Sunbird
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident, highly active during spring flowering (Feb-May). The size of the bird is 11-13 cm. Small, active nectar-feeder with a down-curved bill. Dimorphism: Males are brilliantly colored with iridescent metallic plumage; females are dull olive-green/yellowish.

name: Crow-billed Drongo
description: Assam Seasonality: A year-round resident or summer breeding visitor (April to September). Measures 27–29 cm. Glossy black overall with a deeply forked tail. It is distinguished from other black drongos by its massive, thick, heavily arched "crow-like" bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Dark-necked Tailorbird
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in dense undergrowth and forest edges. Measures 11–12 cm. Bright olive-green back, yellowish belly, and a bright rufous (reddish) crown. Often holds its tail cocked upward. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male in breeding plumage has a prominent blackish patch on the lower throat and upper breast. The female lacks this patch, having a plain whitish throat.

name: Dark-rumped Swift
description: Presence in Assam: Rare summer visitor, occasionally seen foraging over the hills of Assam. Identification: Measures 17-20 cm. A fast-flying, scythe-winged swift. It is entirely blackish-brown with a slightly paler, heavily streaked throat. Crucially, it completely lacks the white rump patch seen in almost all other similar swifts in the region. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Dark-sided Flycatcher
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor and passage migrant (September to April). Measures 13–14 cm. Dark slaty-brown upperparts with a white throat and belly. Its key field mark is heavy, dark smudging on the flanks and sides of the breast, which leaves a single clean, distinct white stripe running right down the center of the belly. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Dark-sided Thrush
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident, highly secretive, living in the dark, damp undergrowth of broadleaved forests. Measures 24–25 cm. A cryptic, ground-dwelling thrush. Rich dark brown above, with heavily scalloped/scaly brown-and-white underparts. It is notable for its exceptionally long, dark bill (much longer than other thrushes). Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Daurian Redstart
description: Assam Seasonality: Common winter visitor (October to March). Measures 14–15 cm. Both sexes feature a very prominent white wing patch (visible when resting and flying) and a rusty-orange tail. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has a silvery-grey crown, black face and back, and bright orange underparts. The female is a uniform, soft brown with a paler belly, but still shows the white wing patch and orange tail.

name: Delicate Prinia / Graceful Prinia

name: Dunlin
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare winter visitor to muddy shores and wetlands, typically between November and March. Measures 16–22 cm. A medium-small, rather hunched sandpiper. Male vs. Female: Visually similar, but the female generally has a noticeably longer bill than the male.

name: Dusky Eagle Owl

name: Dusky Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly winter visitors (October to April) originating from the Himalayas/Siberia. The size of the bird is 10-13 cm. Small, active, cryptic insectivore. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical in most species; identified mainly by vocalizations.

name: Eared Grebe or Black-necked Grebe

Small aquatic diving bird with a slender slightly upturned bill and steep forehead. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; both share the grey/white non-breeding plumage in winter (lacking the golden ear tufts of summer).

name: Eastern Red-rumped Swallow
description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread resident and summer visitor. Measures 18–19 cm. Dark metallic blue upperparts with a striking pale reddish-orange rump patch (visible in flight). The underparts are pale buff and heavily streaked with fine dark lines. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Eastern Spot-billed Duck
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare winter visitor to wetlands and large rivers, generally seen from November to March. (Note: It is easily confused with the very common, year-round resident Indian Spot-billed Duck). Identification: Measures 55–63 cm. A large, dark dabbling duck. It has a pale greyish head and neck with a distinct dark crown and a heavy dark stripe passing directly through the eye. The bill is entirely black with a bright yellow tip. It lacks the distinctive bright red spots at the base of the bill that the resident Indian Spot-billed Duck possesses. Male vs. Female: Sexes are visually very similar, though males are generally slightly larger.

name: Eastern Yellow Wagtail
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor (Oct-Apr) common in wet pastures, marshes, and riverbanks. The size of the bird is 15-17 cm. Dimorphism: Male shows brighter yellow underparts and more distinct head patterns; female is paler and washed-out.

name: Egyptian Vulture

name: Eurasian Curlew
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare winter visitor to large, deep freshwater lakes and open wetlands.. The size of the bird is 50-60 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

description: Presence in Assam: Passage migrant and winter visitor to shaded forest floors and wooded edges (September to April). Identification: Measures 16–18 cm. name: Golden bush Robin
description: Assam Seasonality: No recent records. Mostly winter visitor, descending from the Himalayas to lower foothills (November to March). Measures 14–15 cm. A small, active understory bird. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male is stunning, with bright golden-yellow/orange underparts, a bright yellow eyebrow (supercilium), and an olive-brown back. The female is duller olive overall with a paler yellow wash below and a much fainter eyebrow.

name: Golden headed Cisticola
description: Assam Seasonality: Active winter visitor in Assam's grasslands. The size of the bird is 10-12 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Golden Oriole

A bright, thrush-sized canopy bird with a reddish bill. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male is brilliant, glowing golden-yellow with stark black wings, a black tail and a black eye-stripe that extends just behind the eye. The female is yellowish-green above and pale below with distinct dark streaking on her breast and belly.

name: Golden-crested Myna
description: Presence in Assam: Year-round resident or winter migrant, highly localized to specific broadleaved evergreen forests (such as in Dima Hasao and Cachar). Identification: Measures 22–24 cm. A glossy black myna with a brilliant, golden-yellow patch on the crown/crest, a yellow throat, and a large yellow wing patch visible in flight. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has extensive yellow on the crown, while the female has a much smaller yellow crest, often restricted just to the front of the head.

name: Golden-fronted Leafbird
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 18-21 cm. description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in broadleaved foothill and montane forests; highly vocal with a wailing call. The size of the bird is 31-35 cm. Largest barbet; large pale bill, dark blue head, brown back, and yellow/green underparts. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes look identical.

name: Great Cormorant
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 80-100 cm. name: Great Hornbill
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in low-to-mid elevation evergreen forests. Visible year-round; moves locally tracking fruiting figs. The size of the bird is 95-130 cm. Massive black-and-white hornbill with a huge yellow-and-black u-shaped casque on the bill. Dimorphism: Male has a black iris and black lines on the front of the casque; female is slightly smaller with a striking blood-red iris and no black on the casque front.

name: Great Myna
description: Assam Seasonality: Very common permanent resident across all habitats. The size of the bird is 24-28 cm. Robust, highly vocal omnivorous bird with sturdy yellow or pale legs. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Great Slaty Woodpecker
description: Assam Seasonality: Permanent forest resident across Assam. The size of the bird is 45-58 cm. Strong chisel-like bill, stiff tail feathers for climbing tree trunks. Dimorphism: Males typically possess a bright red crown/crest; females have black crowns with white spots or reduced red.

name: Great Thick-knee
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains, typically patrolling the sandy and rocky banks of major river systems like the Brahmaputra. The size of the bird is 49–55 cm. It has grayish-sandy brown upperparts and a massive, slightly upturned black bill with a yellow base. Look for the prominent white patch encircling the eye — contrasted against black ear-coverts, it gives the bird a distinct spectacled appearance. Male vs. Female:Monomorphic. Both sexes share the same plumage and size.

name: Great White Pelican
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare Winter Migrant on inland water bodies. The size of the bird is 140-180 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Great-eared Nightjar
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare year-round resident in the foothills, favoring forested edges and clearings where it hunts insects at dusk. Measures 31–41 cm. The largest nightjar in the region. It is beautifully camouflaged with intricate patterns of buff, brown, and black, resembling dead leaves. It is unmistakable due to prominent, upright feather tufts on its head that look like "ears." Male vs. Female: Sexes are visually similar.

name: Greater Adjutant
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident and localized breeder. Moves around urban landfills (Guwahati) and nesting colonies from September to April. The size of the bird is 120-152 cm. Massive, prehistoric-looking stork with a thick wedge-shaped bill, dark grey upperparts, a naked pinkish head/neck, and a distinctive low-hanging inflatable throat pouch. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical in plumage, but males average slightly larger with longer, heavier bills.

name: Greater Coucal
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 43-48 cm. name: Greater Flameback
description: Assam Seasonality: Permanent forest resident across Assam. The size of the bird is 33-36 cm. Strong chisel-like bill, stiff tail feathers for climbing tree trunks. Dimorphism: Males typically possess a bright red crown/crest; females have black crowns with white spots or reduced red.

name: Greater Painted Snipe
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident, quietly hiding in heavily vegetated swamps, marshes and flooded paddy fields. Identification: Measures 23–28 cm. A distinctively marked, secretive wader with a relatively short, slightly drooping bill and a large dark eye framed by a striking white or buff "spectacle" (a ring around the eye extending into a stripe behind it). Male vs. Female: Exhibits reverse sexual dimorphism (the female is larger and more colorful than the male). The female has a rich, dark chestnut head and neck, a solid black breast band and dark bronze-green wings. The male is smaller and much duller, heavily mottled in grey-brown to blend into the reeds, and features prominent pale buff "suspenders" (stripes over the shoulders).

name: Greater Racket-tailed Drongo
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident; conspicuous perching on open branches.  size of the bird is 31-40 cm(upto 65 incl. rackets). Glossy black plumage with a distinctively forked or modified tail. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes are identical.

name: Greater Scaup
description: Presence in Assam: A very rare winter visitor to large rivers and lakes (December to February). Identification: Measures 39–56 cm. A medium-sized diving duck with a large, rounded head and grey bill. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has a pale grey back, white sides, a black breast and a dark head that glows with a green iridescent sheen in good light. The female is mostly brown with a highly distinct, broad white ring of feathers around the base of her bill.

name: Greater Short-toed Lark
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor to dry, open plains and stubble fields from October to March. Identification: Measures 13–14 cm. A small, pale sandy-brown lark. It has streaked upperparts and clean, unstreaked pale underparts. Its most distinctive mark is a dark patch on either side of its neck (though this can sometimes be difficult to see). Male vs. Female: Sexes are visually similar.

name: Greater Spotted Eagle
description: Assam Seasonality: Vulnerable. Winter visitor frequenting large marshes, wetlands, and open riverine tracts. The size of the bird is 59-71 cm. Large, dark, heavily built eagle with a short tail and broad wings. Dimorphism: Monomorphic; sexes look identical, but females are slightly larger in wingspan and bulk.

name: Greater White-fronted Goose
description: Assam Seasonality: Rare winter visitor to major wetlands and river sandbars (November to March). Measures 65–78 cm. A large, greyish-brown goose. Adults are uniquely identified by a distinct white patch on the front of the face right at the base of a pinkish/orange bill, and heavy, irregular black barring across the belly. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Greater Yellownape
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in mature broadleaved forests. Measures 33–34 cm. A large, vibrant olive-green woodpecker with a massive, brilliant golden-yellow crest on the nape (back of the neck) and a plain yellowish-olive belly. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male features a bright yellow throat and a rufous-brown malar (cheek) stripe. The female has a rufous-brown throat and lacks the bright yellow throat patch.

name: Greater-Necklaced Laughingthrush
description: Assam Seasonality: Highly sedentary year-round resident. The size of the bird is 27-30 cm. Gregarious forest/undergrowth bird with strong legs, operating in noisy social flocks. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical.

name: Green Cochoa
description: Presence in Assam: A very rare resident in the dense canopies of broadleaved hill forests; highly secretive and rarely seen. Identification: Measures 24-26 cm. A stunning, thrush-like bird. It has bright, moss-green body plumage with a silvery-blue crown. Its most spectacular feature is a patch of brilliant silvery-blue on the wings and tail. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has bright silvery-blue wing patches and a blackish mask. The female has the same green body but her wing patches are a dull brownish-yellow rather than blue.

name: Green Imperial-Pigeon
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident across agricultural and forest zones. The size of the bird is 40-45 cm. Plump body, short neck, slender bill with a fleshy cere. Dimorphism: Most species are similar, though males can be slightly glossier or display more intense color patches.

name: Green Sandpiper
description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread winter visitor to wetlands, ponds, and small streams (August to April). Measures 21–24 cm. A medium-sized, dark wader. Its upperparts are dark olive-brown finely speckled with white; underparts are brilliant white. In flight, it shows completely dark underwings and a striking white rump that contrasts heavily with its dark tail. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Greenish Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly winter visitors (October to April) originating from the Himalayas/Siberia. The size of the bird is 10-12 cm. Small, active, cryptic insectivore. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical in most species; identified mainly by vocalizations.

name: Grey Bushchat
description: Assam Seasonality: Common winter visitor across scrublands and edges (October to April); resident in higher hills. Measures 15 cm. Frequently sits upright on exposed perches like fences or bush tops. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male has dark slaty-grey upperparts, a black face mask, a distinct white eyebrow, and a variable rusty wash on the breast. The female is warm brown above with a paler belly, completely lacking the sharp black-and-grey contrast of the male.

name: Grey Heron

description: Assam Seasonality: Rare year-round resident in wooded hills, ravines, and forest edges. Measures 36–40 cm. A slender, long-tailed bird in the crow family. It has an ashy-grey body, warm brown back, and a black face/throat mask. The wings are black with a prominent white patch visible when it flies. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Grey Wagtail
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor; commonly seen from September to April near rocky streams and rivers. Measures 18–19 cm. A sleek, slender bird with a conspicuously long tail that it bobs constantly. It has slate-grey upperparts, a distinct white supercilium (eyebrow), and bright yellow underparts (especially under the tail). Male vs. Female: Dimorphic primarily in breeding plumage. The breeding male develops a striking black throat, which the female lacks (her throat remains whitish/pale buff). In winter, both sexes look very similar with white throats, but males may show traces of black.

name: Grey-backed Shrike
description: Assam Seasonality: Widespread; some are winter visitors (Oct-April). The size of the bird is 24-26 cm. Hooked carnivorous bill, distinct black eye-mask. Dimorphism: Males have starker, darker masks; females often show faint scalloping on underparts.

name: Grey-bellied Cuckoo
description: Assam Seasonality: Summer breeding visitor and passage migrant; typically seen from April to September. Measures 23 cm. A medium size, slim cuckoo. Adults are mostly dark grey above and pale grey below, with a distinctive white vent/undertail and white barring underneath the tail. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. Males are uniformly grey. Females have two morphs: a grey morph similar to the male, and a "hepatic" (liver) morph which is bright rufous-brown above and heavily barred with dark brown across the entire body.

name: Grey-bellied Tesia
description: Presence in Assam: Resident in the dark undergrowth of wet hill forests. Identification: Measures 8–10 cm. A tiny, hyperactive, virtually tailless bird that looks like a little bouncing ball. It has bright olive-green upperparts and dark slaty-grey underparts. It features a distinct yellowish-green eyebrow and a dark eye-stripe. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar.

name: Grey-breasted Prinia
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident, frequently found in scrub, tall grass, and secondary growth. Measures 11–13 cm. A small, active warbler. Male vs. Female: Sexes are generally similar, though the male in breeding plumage shows a bolder, darker grey breast band and a blackish bill compared to the female's paler band and lighter bill.

A noticeable greyish lore (area between eye and bill) runs across the face. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The female features a narrow, incomplete silvery-white breast band that the male completely lacks.

name: Grey-sided Bush Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor descending from the Himalayas to scrub and grassy edges from November to March. Measures 10–11 cm. A very small, skulking warbler. name: Rufous-throated Partridge
description: No recent records are found. Year-round resident in the dense undergrowth of hill forests. Male vs. Female: Females are similar to males but are generally duller with less pronounced throat patterns.

name: Russet Bush Warbler
description: Presence in Assam: Resident in the hills, moving to lower elevations and tall grassy plains in winter. Identification: Measures 13–14 cm. A skulking, dark russet-brown warbler. It has a white throat that contrasts sharply with a dark, mottled grey-brown breast band and warm reddish-brown upperparts. Usually identified by its mechanical, buzzy song. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Russet Sparrow
description: Presence in Assam: No recent records are found. Resident in the hills, moving to lower valleys and foothills in the winter (November to March). Identification: Measures 14–15 cm. A brightly colored sparrow found in open forests and agricultural edges. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. The male has a vibrant, rich chestnut-red (russet) crown and back, a black throat bib, and a yellowish wash on the belly. The female looks similar to a female House Sparrow with a heavily streaked brown back, but is distinguished by a very prominent pale whitish eyebrow (supercilium) and a faint yellowish wash on the belly.

name: Rusty-bellied Shortwing
description: Presence in Assam: Rare resident in the dark, dense undergrowth of hill forests, sometimes moving slightly lower in winter. Identification: Measures 12–13 cm. A small, skulking, almost tailless bird that hops on the forest floor. It has a distinct white eyebrow (supercilium) and black bill. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. The male is deep slaty-blue above with rich, rusty-orange underparts. The female is olive-brown above and paler rusty-buff below, lacking the blue.

name: Sand lark
description: Assam Seasonality: A winter visitor, almost strictly confined to the sandy banks and islands of the Brahmaputra River. A small lark (12–13 cm) that is very pale and sandy-grey — offering perfect camouflage against river sand. It has a short, stubby bill and fine, crisp streaking on the breast. Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical.

name: Sapphire Flycatcher

The female is warm olive-brown above with a duller orange wash on the breast and a rusty-colored tail, completely lacking any blue.

name: Sarus Crane (Not found/Extinct from Assam)

Dimorphism: Males have a striking golden-yellow crown; females have an olive-green crown matching the back.

description: Assam Seasonality: Mix of altitudinal summer breeders and winter migrants. The size of the bird is 12-14 cm. Small upright-perching insectivore that sally-catches flies. Dimorphism: Strikingly dimorphic; males are brightly colored (blue, orange, or white), females are dull brown/grey.

name: Slaty-breasted rail
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in marshes, flooded fields, and wetlands. A secretive water bird (25–27 cm). Male vs. Female: Females are slightly duller than males, with less extensive grey on the breast.

description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor and highly localized resident in the hills. Identification: Measures 26-28 cm. Looks almost exactly like the Black-naped Oriole (yellow with a black band around the back of the head). However, the black band is noticeably narrower, and its pinkish bill is distinctly longer, thinner, and slightly downcurved compared to other orioles. Male vs. Female: Slightly dimorphic. Females are slightly greener on the back than the golden-yellow males.

description: Assam Seasonality: A very rare winter visitor to major rivers and wetlands (November to February). A small, compact diving duck (38–44 cm) with a short, serrated bill. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. Males are stunningly white with a bold black mask around the eye and a black "V" on the back. Females (often called "redheads") have a grey body with a sharply contrasting chestnut-red head and a bright white cheek patch.

name: smoky Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor (November to March), preferring low vegetation near wetlands. A small, rather dark warbler (11–12 cm). It has dark brownish-olive upperparts, a dusky/smoky-grey underside, and a prominent dark eyestripe contrasting with a pale yellowish supercilium (eyebrow). Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical.

name: Snowy-browed Flycatcher
description: Assam Seasonality: Primarily a winter visitor to the plains and foot-hills, though some may be altitudinal residents in the higher hills. A tiny, short-tailed flycatcher (11–12 cm). Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. Males have slaty-blue upperparts, bright rusty-orange underparts, and a very distinct, bright white short eyebrow. Females are drab olive-brown above and pale buffy below, lacking the slaty blue and the white brow.

description: Assam Seasonality: No recent records are available. An extremely rare, accidental vagrant. This species strictly prefers coastal mudflats, so any inland sighting in Assam is exceptional and highly noteworthy. Measures 14–16 cm. A tiny wader that looks very much like a Little Stint in its pale grey-and-white winter plumage. It is entirely unique due to its bill: the tip flares out into a distinct, flat, diamond-shaped "spoon" or spatula. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: Spot-bellied Eagle Owl
description: Assam Seasonality: Permanent nocturnal resident. The size of the bird is 50-65 cm. Nocturnal predator with a large facial disc, forward-facing eyes, and silent flight. Dimorphism: Plumage is identical; females are frequently larger and heavier.

name: Spot-billed Pelican
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitors on inland water bodies. The size of the bird is 125-152 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: Spot-winged Starling
description: Assam Seasonality: Rare winter visitor or year-round resident; highly nomadic and usually seen in flowering or fruiting canopy trees. A medium-sized starling (19–20 cm) with a relatively slender body and pale eyes. Male vs. Female: Males have brownish-grey upperparts, a dark facial mask, and heavily scaly, rufous-tinged underparts with a white wing patch. Females are much plainer and browner, lacking the distinct dark mask and rich scaly breast.

name: Spotted Dove
description: Assam Seasonality: Very common year-round resident across agricultural and forest zones. The size of the bird is 28-32 cm. Plump body, short neck, slender bill with a fleshy cere. Dimorphism: Most species are similar, though males can be slightly glossier or display more intense color patches.

name: Spotted Forktail
description: Assam Seasonality: A rare bird for the plains. Year-round resident along fast-flowing, rocky streams in the hills. A large, elegant bird (25–28 cm) with a deeply forked, long tail. It is starkly black and white, easily identified by the heavy white spotting on its black back and a white forehead patch. Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical.

description: Assam Seasonality: Summer visitor and resident in broadleaved forests. About the size of a bulbul (25 cm), this bird perfectly mimics a small drongo. It is entirely glossy black with a slightly forked or square-tipped tail. The best field mark is its slightly downcurved cuckoo bill, which differs from a drongo's stout bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are mostly similar, but the female may be slightly duller black.

name: Steepe Eagle
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor to open country and garbage dumps (October to April). Identification: Measures 62–81 cm. A large, uniformly dark brown eagle. A key identification feature is its very wide mouth (gape) with a yellow fleshy line that extends backward past the eye. Male vs. Female: Visually similar with the female being larger.

description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor in tall wet grasslands and reeds. A very large, conspicuous warbler-like bird (22–28 cm). It has a heavily dark-streaked brown back, streaked breast, and a very long, graduated, ragged-looking tail. Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical.

name: Streak-breasted Scimiter Babbler
description: Assam Seasonality: No recent records are found. A year-round resident in dense hill forests and bamboo brakes. A medium babbler (19 cm) characterized by a long, sharply downcurved yellowish bill. It has olive-brown upperparts, a stark white eyebrow, a black mask, and a white throat/breast heavily streaked with olive-brown. Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical.

name: Streak-throated Woodpecker
description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in open woodlands and forest edges. A medium-sized green woodpecker (30 cm). Females have a completely blackish crown with no red.

name: Tibetan Sand Plover
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor to major river sandbars (October to April). Identification: Measures 19–21 cm. A compact, greyish wader. During breeding (rarely seen in Assam), males develop a bold black face mask and a broad, bright rufous-orange breast band, which the females lack or show only very faintly.

name: Tickell's Leaf Warbler
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly winter visitors (October to April) originating from the Himalayas/Siberia. The size of the bird is 10-13 cm. Small, active, cryptic insectivore. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical in most species; identified mainly by vocalizations.

name: Timminck's Stint
description: Assam Seasonality: Winter visitor (September to May) to muddy margins of wetlands and rivers. A tiny wader (13–15 cm). In winter, it is plain greyish-brown above and white below, with a distinctive uniform greyish wash across the breast. A key feature is its pale yellowish or greenish legs (unlike the black legs of the Little Stint). Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical in winter.

description: Presence in Assam: Resident or sessional migraint in Assam, a very handful of records are available till now; occurring in suitable grassland habitats, wetlands, marshes, reed beds and cultivated areas. The adult has a distinctive combination of black, chestnut-brown, and white plumage. The head, throat, and upper breast are black, the back and wings are chestnut-brown and the underparts are predominantly white with a black patch in the centre of the belly and dark undertail coverts. Male vs. Female: Sexes are similar in appearance, with no obvious differences in plumage.

name: Tufted Duck
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly winter visitors on inland water bodies. The size of the bird is 40-47 cm. Aquatic waterfowl with webbed feet and a flattened bill. Dimorphism: Strongly dimorphic in breeding season; males display bright ornamental plumage, females are cryptically mottled brown.

name: Ultramarine Flycatcher
description: Presence in Assam: Very rare winter visitor to open forests and edges (October to March). Identification: Measures 11–12 cm. A small, active flycatcher. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. The male is deep, rich blue on the upperparts with a brilliant white breast and belly and a stark white supercilium (eyebrow). The female is completely different: drab greyish-brown above, pale whitish below, lacking any blue.

description: Assam Seasonality: Year-round resident in woodlands and orchards. The size of the bird is 13-14 cm. Green plumage, strongly hooked red bill, zygodactyl feet. Dimorphism: Adult males feature distinct neck rings or head patches absent in females.

name: Violet Cuckoo
description: Assam Seasonality: Summer breeding visitor and resident in tropical broadleaved forests. A very small cuckoo (17 cm). Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. Males are stunning — highly glossy violet-purple on the head, back, and upper breast, with a white belly heavily barred with dark purple. Females look completely different: they are bronze-green above with a dark crown, and heavily barred with green and white below.

name: Wallcreeper
description: Assam Seasonality: A scarce winter visitor from the high Himalayas, found from November to March. It is highly specialized and almost exclusively seen clinging to vertical rock faces, steep river gorges, and occasionally brick walls or quarries. Identification: Measures 15.5–17 cm. A small, incredibly unique bird with a long, thin, downcurved black bill used for extracting insects from rock crevices. Male vs. Female: Dimorphic primarily during the breeding season. In winter (when they visit Assam), both sexes look very similar, possessing a whitish throat and breast. During the summer breeding season in the high mountains, the male develops a solid black throat and upper breast, while the female's throat remains pale or only slightly dusky.

name: Water Rail
description: Presence in Assam: Winter visitor to dense reedbeds and marshes (November to March). Identification: Measures 23–28 cm. A highly secretive, laterally compressed marsh bird. It has heavily streaked brown upperparts, a slaty-blue face and breast, heavily black-and-white barred flanks and a long, slightly downcurved red bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are visually similar.

Male vs. Female: Males have a distinct maroon-red wash on the back/shoulders and a vibrant orange-rufous wash on the crown and breast. Male vs. Female: Sexes look identical.

name: White Wagtail
description: Assam Seasonality: Mostly winter visitors (Oct-April) found in grasslands and riverbanks. The size of the bird is 14-19 cm. Slender terrestrial bird that walks on the ground and constantly pumps its tail. Dimorphism: Sexes are largely identical.

name: White-bellied Heron

Identification: Measures 127 cm. The second-largest heron in the world. It is incredibly tall and mostly dark slaty-grey with a distinctively long neck and a very thick, dark greyish-black bill. It gets its name from a contrasting pure white belly and white under-wing coverts visible in flight. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: White-breasted Waterhen
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident. The size of the bird is 30-33 cm. Distinctive local avian species with regional field marks. Dimorphism: Sexes vary; males frequently show brighter plumage during the spring breeding cycle.

name: White-browed fantail
description: Presence in Assam: Year-round resident, mostly in open woodlands, scrub and gardens of the plains. Identification: Measures 17–18 cm. A highly active bird that constantly dances through the foliage, fanning its tail to flush insects. It has dark slaty-brown upperparts, white underparts with dark spotting on the chest, a very broad white forehead and eyebrow and a tail tipped heavily with white. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical.

name: White-browed Piculet
description: Assam Seasonality: Active year-round resident or seasonal migrant in Assam's diverse floodplains and forest layers. The size of the bird is 8-10 cm. It is boldly patterned in stark black and white. Its entire head, back and breast are black, contrasting with a clean white belly. Its most striking feature is a very broad, prominent white eyebrow (supercilium). Male vs. Female: Slightly dimorphic. The female's black plumage is often slightly duller or more greyish-black compared to the male's glossy jet-black.

name: White-tailed Eagle
description: Presence in Assam: A very rare winter vagrant, occasionally spotted near major, undisturbed wetlands and the Brahmaputra River (November to March). Identification: Measures 66–94 cm with a massive wingspan up to 2.4 meters. A gargantuan, broad-winged eagle. Adults have a pale head and neck, a dark brown body, a massive, blocky yellow bill and a striking, short, pure white, wedge-shaped tail. Male vs. Female: Visually similar in plumage, but the female is noticeably larger and bulkier than the male.

name: White-tailed Robin
description: Assam Seasonality: Resident in the dark, dense undergrowth of hill forests. A small, secretive, ground-dwelling bird (17–19 cm). Both sexes flash distinct white patches at the base of the outer tail feathers when they flick their tails. Male vs. Female: Highly dimorphic. Males are deep, inky blackish-blue overall with a concealed silvery-blue brow. Females are uniform olive-brown with a pale throat and the same white tail patches.

name: White-tailed Stonechat
description: Assam Seasonality: A winter visitor, almost exclusively found in tall wet grasslands and river islands (Brahmaputra floodplains). A small, upright-perching bird (13–14 cm). Male vs. Female: Dimorphic. Males have a black head and back, a rusty-orange breast, and extensive white patches on the collar, wings, and inner tail feathers. Females are streaky brown above and pale buff below, lacking the striking black and prominent white patches.

name: White-throated Bulbul
description: Assam Seasonality: Common year-round resident in forests. The size of the bird is 18-22 cm. Medium-sized songbird with short crest or distinct vent coloring. Dimorphism: Sexes are identical (monomorphic); juveniles are slightly duller.

Dimorphism: Sexes are generally similar, but males are significantly larger and heavier; females have more densely speckled heads and necks.

It has a very long, straight bill. Male vs. Female: Sexes are identical in plumage and size.

name: Yellow-vented Warbler

name: Yellow-wattled Lapwing
description: Assam Seasonality: This species prefers dry, arid open habitats (like dry stubble fields and barren wastelands). Its most recognizable features are a solid black cap (crown) on top of its head and striking, bright yellow fleshy wattles (flaps of skin) hanging directly in front of its eyes.
